q: 准备 AI 编码面试最有效的一件事是什么？
q_en: What is the most effective way to prepare for an AI coding interview?
options: 反复阅读面试经验帖，但从不真正动手做题
找一道真实题目，按面试时长完整做完并拿到反馈
把常用提示词模板背下来，面试直接照搬
看别人打比赛、解题的录像，自己不动手
options_en: Repeatedly reading interview-experience posts without ever actually doing a problem.
Pick a real problem, finish it under real interview time, and get feedback on it.
Memorize a set of go-to prompt templates and reuse them verbatim in the interview.
Watch other people's solve recordings without practicing yourself.
why: 唯一能同时练到问题拆解、AI 驱动、验证和沟通四项能力的，是完整做题并拿到反馈；反馈能精确指出面试前该补哪一项。
why_en: Full practice with feedback works best because it trains problem breakdown, AI control, verification, and communication together, then points at what to fix.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Practice[Full practice] --> Record[Capture prompts]
  Record --> Feedback[Get feedback]
  Feedback --> Fix[Pick one weakness]
  Fix --> Practice

termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

把准备等同于旁观别人操作而不亲自动手。

Treats prep as running the full workflow under real constraints and reviewing it.
Treats prep as memorizing a script you can copy verbatim.
Treats prep as watching someone else operate instead of doing it yourself.

完整走一遍能暴露拆解、驱动 AI、验证、沟通各环节的真实短板。
话术遇到具体代码库时套不上，反而暴露背诵痕迹。
看别人操作学不到自己动手时的判断和失误模式。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: No amount of reading trains the real dual-conversation and verification rhythm.
A full run surfaces real gaps in breakdown, AI control, verification, and communication.
Canned phrasing breaks against a real codebase and reveals itself as rote.
Watching others can't teach the judgment and mistakes you only hit by doing it yourself.

最直接；它是唯一同时覆盖四项评估维度并带反馈的做法。

不直接；旁观不能训练你自己的判断。

Most direct — it is the only approach that covers all four evaluation areas with feedback.
Not direct — a fixed script tends to fail against an unfamiliar codebase.
Not direct — watching cannot train your own judgment.

scenario: AI 编码面试练习平台把练习分成两条通道：一条给你 clone 仓库到本地写代码，另一条直接在浏览器沙盒里用平台自带 AI 分阶段出题。
scenario_en: An AI coding interview practice platform offers two tracks: one has you clone a repo and code locally, while the other puts you in a browser sandbox with the platform's built-in AI and staged prompts.
q: 这两条练习通道分别复刻了哪两类真实面试现场？
q_en: Which two real interview settings do these practice tracks recreate?
options: 两条通道都只对应纯电话面试，没有实质差别
开放式对应算法笔试网站，结构化对应系统设计画图
开放式对应 BYOE 屏幕共享面试，结构化对应平台内置 AI 面试
开放式对应现场白板面试，结构化对应邮件异步面试
options_en: Both tracks only correspond to plain phone screens, with no real difference.
Open-ended corresponds to algorithm quiz sites, structured corresponds to system-design whiteboarding.
Open-ended corresponds to BYOE screen-share interviews, structured corresponds to platform interviews with built-in AI.
Open-ended corresponds to in-person whiteboard interviews, structured corresponds to async email interviews.
why: 开放式通道复刻用自己编辑器、AI 工具屏幕共享的面试；结构化通道复刻 CoderPad/HackerRank 式内置 AI 的分阶段面试。
why_en: The open-ended track mirrors BYOE screen-share interviews with your own tools, while the structured track mirrors phased CoderPad/HackerRank-style interviews with built-in AI.
tradeoff: 复刻自带工具的 BYOE 面试 vs 复刻平台内置 AI 的结构化面试

scenario: 你的目标公司允许使用自己的 IDE 和日常 AI 工具，并让你屏幕共享从仓库开始构建。
scenario_en: Your target company lets you use your own IDE and daily AI tools while screen-sharing as you build from a repo.
q: 该优先练哪种练习方式？
q_en: Which practice format should you prioritize?
options: 先在结构化浏览器沙盒里适应平台内置 AI
只精读该公司过往面试真题，不动手写代码
用在线协作文档记录解题思路，不实际提交代码
clone 仓库，按真实时长计时，用自己工具独立完成并提交反馈
options_en: Warm up in a structured browser sandbox to get used to the platform's built-in AI.
Only re-read this company's past interview questions without writing any code.
Jot down your approach in a shared doc without actually submitting runnable code.
Clone the repo, time yourself for real, finish independently with your own tools, then submit for feedback.
why: 目标公司走 BYOE 屏幕共享，练习就该照搬你会用到的编辑器、AI 工具和真实计时，而不是先去适应平台沙盒。
why_en: Because the target interview is BYOE screen-share, you should practice with your own editor, AI tools, and real timing instead of a platform sandbox.
whenOtherWins: 如果目标公司明确使用 CoderPad 或 HackerRank，结构化沙盒反而更贴近当天体验。
tradeoff: 复刻自己工具的真实工作流 vs 提前适应平台内置沙盒

why: 结构化沙盒和 CoderPad/HackerRank 平台内置 AI 高度相似，提前适应能减少正式面试当天的工具摩擦。

text: 开放式练习会给你 clone repo 的命令，配合真实面试长度的{{计时器}}；完成后上传{{代码}}和{{AI 聊天}}获得反馈。

q: 系统给出的反馈通常基于哪些材料？（多选）
q_en: What materials does the system usually use for feedback? (Select all that apply.)
options: 你提交的代码
你和 AI 的聊天记录
hire/no-hire 评级和具体改进建议
你对目标薪资的期望
options_en: The code you submitted.
Your chat transcript with the AI.
A hire/no-hire rating plus concrete suggestions for improvement.
Your target salary expectations.
why: 反馈要同时评估成品和过程，尤其是你是否在聊天记录里体现了对 AI 的控制力，而不只是最终代码能不能跑。
why_en: Feedback covers both the final code and the AI chat log because reviewers check whether you stayed in control of the AI, not just whether the code runs.

why: CoderPad/HackerRank 这类平台体验和日常 IDE 差异很大，提前适应能把当天注意力留给题目而不是工具。

scenario_en: You are not sure whether the target company uses an open-ended or structured AI interview.
q: 准备策略最稳的选择是什么？
q_en: What is the safest preparation strategy?
options: 只练你更熟悉的本地环境，赌面试是开放式
只练结构化浏览器沙盒，赌面试是平台面试
两种格式都至少完整练一次，降低猜错的风险
完全不做任何练习，等到面试当天临场应变
options_en: Only practice your familiar local setup and bet the interview is open-ended.
Only practice the structured browser sandbox and bet it's a platform interview.
Do at least one full practice run in both formats to cut the risk of guessing wrong.
Skip practice entirely and improvise on interview day.
why: 格式不确定时，两边都至少练一次能把猜错格式的风险降到最低，代价是要多花一次练习的时间。
why_en: When the target format is unknown, practicing both at least once minimizes the risk of guessing the wrong environment, at the cost of extra practice time.
whenOtherWins: 如果 recruiter 已经明确格式，就该把主要时间集中在对应环境上，不必平均分配。
tradeoff: 两边都练降低猜错风险 vs 押注一边省练习时间
optionMeanings: 把赌注押在开放式，风险自担。
把赌注押在结构化，风险自担。
用两次练习换取对冲两种格式的确定性。
把整场准备寄托在临场发挥上。
optionMeanings_en: Bets everything on open-ended and accepts the risk.
Bets everything on structured and accepts the risk.
Spends two practice runs to hedge against either format.
Bets the entire preparation on improvising on the day.
optionScenarioImpacts: 如果面试其实是结构化，平台摩擦会当场暴露。
如果面试其实是开放式，本地工具反而生疏。
不管落在哪种格式，工具都已经练过一遍。
两种环境都陌生，风险最高。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: If the interview turns out structured, platform friction shows up on the day.
If the interview turns out open-ended, your local tools end up rusty instead.
Whichever format it turns out to be, you've already rehearsed the tools.
Both environments stay unfamiliar, which is the highest-risk option.
optionDirectness: 不直接；押注一半概率会猜错。
不直接；同样是押注，代价对称。
最直接；直接消除格式不确定带来的风险。
不直接；完全放弃了降低风险的机会。
optionDirectness_en: Not direct — betting has roughly even odds of being wrong.
Not direct — an equally symmetric bet with the same downside.
Most direct — it directly removes the risk created by format uncertainty.
Not direct — it gives up the chance to reduce risk at all.

scenario: 你刚开始准备 AI 编码面试，还没熟悉双线沟通和 AI 验证节奏。
scenario_en: You are just starting AI coding interview prep and are not yet used to the rhythm of dual communication and AI verification.
q: 第一轮练习更适合怎么选题？
q_en: How should you choose a problem for your first practice round?
options: 直接选列表里最难的一题，模拟最大压力
只读题目描述，不实际提交代码
只看别人的解题记录，不自己动手
先从 Easy 或熟悉的 Medium 起步，跑顺完整流程
options_en: Jump straight to the hardest problem on the list to simulate max pressure.
Only read the problem statement without actually submitting code.
Only watch other people's solve recordings without practicing yourself.
Start with Easy or a familiar Medium problem and get the full workflow smooth.
why: 早期要先把环境、计时、AI 使用和反馈这套流程跑顺，而不是一上来就用最大难度考验自己。
why_en: Early practice should get the full workflow smooth on an easier problem before you push straight to maximum difficulty.
whenOtherWins: 如果流程已经熟悉、目标公司题目又偏难，可以尽快切到 Hard 模拟真实压力。
tradeoff: 先跑顺流程再加难度 vs 一开始就上强度

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

optionMeanings: 把强度当成第一轮练习的首要目标。
把练习简化成阅读，跳过动手环节。
把练习简化成旁观，不训练自己的判断。
把第一轮目标定为跑顺整套工作流。
optionMeanings_en: Treats intensity as the top priority of the first practice round.
Reduces practice to reading, skipping the hands-on part.
Reduces practice to watching, without training your own judgment.
Sets the first round's goal as smoothing out the whole workflow.
optionScenarioImpacts: 难题会同时暴露多个短板，第一轮很难定位问题出在哪。
不写代码就练不到 AI 驱动和验证。
旁观学不到自己动手时的真实失误。
简单题让你专注适应双线沟通和验证节奏本身。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A hard problem exposes many gaps at once, making it hard to isolate the cause.
Skipping code means no practice driving the AI or verifying output.
Watching can't teach the real mistakes you only hit by doing it yourself.
An easier problem lets you focus on the dual-conversation and verification rhythm itself.
optionDirectness: 不直接；难度不是第一轮该优化的变量。
不直接；没有产出就没有可复盘的东西。
不直接；旁观不能替代亲自练习。
最直接；这正是新手第一轮该建立的基础。
optionDirectness_en: Not direct — difficulty isn't the variable to optimize in round one.
Not direct — no output means nothing to review afterward.
Not direct — watching cannot replace hands-on practice.
Most direct — this is exactly the foundation a first-timer should build.

scenario: 你下周面试，目标轮据说会有多阶段和较强优化要求。
scenario_en: Your interview is next week, and the target round is said to include multiple stages and strong optimization requirements.
q: 更合理的练习组合是什么？
q_en: What is a more reasonable practice mix?
options: 只挑最简单的题反复刷，只求熟悉页面操作
至少做一个结构化 Medium，再做一个 Hard 模拟压力
完全不设置计时器，按自己节奏慢慢打磨代码
只刷传统 LeetCode 式 Easy 题，不碰浏览器沙盒
options_en: Only grind the easiest problems, just to get familiar with the page layout.
Do at least one structured Medium, then one Hard to simulate real pressure.
Skip the timer entirely and polish the code at your own pace.
Only grind traditional LeetCode-style Easy problems and skip the browser sandbox.
why: Medium 练节奏，Hard 练优化和复杂约束下的 AI 驱动，两个难度暴露的短板不同，缺一个都补不全。
why_en: A Medium problem builds rhythm while a Hard problem exposes optimization and constraint-handling gaps that a Medium alone won't surface.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试明确是开放式 BYOE，应把同样两档难度放到本地工具链里练，而不是浏览器沙盒。
tradeoff: 覆盖 Medium+Hard 两档暴露不同短板 vs 只练单一难度省时间

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个常见的算法刷题网站，题目多是单函数、无 AI 辅助。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LeetCode is a common algorithm-practice site with single-function problems and no AI assistance.

optionMeanings: 把准备目标停在熟悉界面，难度不够。
用两档难度分别覆盖节奏和优化两类短板。
去掉计时约束，练不出真实压力下的节奏。
难度和环境都和目标面试不匹配。
optionMeanings_en: Caps the goal at getting familiar with the interface, too low a bar.
Uses two difficulty tiers to cover rhythm and optimization separately.
Drops the timing constraint, so it never builds a real-pressure rhythm.
Mismatches both difficulty and environment against the target interview.
optionScenarioImpacts: 多阶段和优化要求下，Easy 题根本练不到相关能力。
Medium 建立节奏，Hard 提前暴露优化短板。
没有计时，正式面试当天的节奏依然是陌生的。
传统 Easy 题不涉及多阶段推进，练错了重点。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Easy problems can't build the skills a multi-stage, optimization-heavy round needs.
Medium builds rhythm; Hard surfaces optimization gaps ahead of time.
Without timing, the real pace of interview day stays unfamiliar.
Traditional Easy problems skip the staged flow, missing the actual focus.
optionDirectness: 不直接；难度远低于目标面试要求。
最直接；两档难度正好对上多阶段+优化的要求。
不直接；计时压力是目标面试的一部分。
不直接；传统 Easy 题覆盖不到结构化多阶段。
optionDirectness_en: Not direct — the difficulty is far below what the target interview needs.
Most direct — two tiers line up exactly with the staged-plus-optimization requirement.
Not direct — timing pressure is part of the target interview.
Not direct — traditional Easy problems don't cover a structured staged flow.

q: 补全结构化练习目标：
q_en: Complete the goal of structured practice:
text: 结构化练习的目标是让 CoderPad/HackerRank 式的{{浏览器编辑器}}、{{内置 AI}}和多阶段推进在正式面试前变得熟悉。
why: 陌生的浏览器编辑器和受限 AI 会占用认知带宽，提前练能把这部分预算腾给真正的问题拆解。
why_en: An unfamiliar browser editor and constrained AI eat into your attention, so practicing in advance frees that budget for actual problem solving.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一款常见的在线协作编程面试平台，内置浏览器代码编辑器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CoderPad is a common online collaborative coding interview platform with a built-in browser editor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 另一款常用的在线编程测评/面试平台，题目按阶段推进。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HackerRank is another common online coding assessment platform that advances problems in stages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

scenario: 你已经按真实时长完成了三道练习题，但每次都直接跳到下一题，没打开反馈报告。
scenario_en: You have completed three practice problems under real timing, but each time you jumped straight to the next one without opening the feedback report.
q: 这样做主要会让你缺失什么？
q_en: What do you mainly miss by doing this?
options: 不知道自己在 AI 控制、验证或沟通上具体哪里失控
不知道这道题的名字叫什么
不知道自己写没写过代码
不知道 AI 助手是否连了网络
options_en: You won't know specifically where your AI control, verification, or communication broke down.
You won't know what the problem is called.
You won't know whether you wrote any code at all.
You won't know whether the AI assistant had network access.
why: 反馈能精确指出你在控制 AI、验证或沟通上的具体弱点；不看反馈，你只能凭感觉猜哪里出了问题。
why_en: Feedback pinpoints exactly where your AI control, verification, or communication broke down; skip it and you're only guessing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

optionMeanings: 准确指出反馈缺失后失去的具体校准信息。
把反馈的价值窄化成记住题目名字。
凭空断言你会忘记自己写没写代码。
把反馈内容错当成检查网络连通性。
optionMeanings_en: Correctly names the specific calibration information you lose without feedback.
Narrows the value of feedback down to remembering the problem's name.
Wrongly assumes you'd forget whether you wrote code at all.
Mistakes the content of feedback for a network-connectivity check.
optionScenarioImpacts: 没有这层信息，下一轮练习不知道该改哪里。
题目名字本来就不是反馈要告诉你的东西。
你自己肯定知道有没有写代码，这不需要靠反馈。
网络状态和你的表现评估无关。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Without this, the next practice round has no clear target to fix.
The problem's name was never something feedback is meant to tell you.
You already know whether you wrote code; feedback isn't needed for that.
Network status has nothing to do with evaluating your performance.
optionDirectness: 最直接；这正是反馈缺失后真正丢掉的信息。
不直接；和反馈的评估目的无关。
不直接；这不需要靠反馈才能知道。
不直接；网络连通性不是反馈评估的内容。
optionDirectness_en: Most direct — this is exactly the information you lose without feedback.
Not direct — unrelated to what feedback is meant to evaluate.
Not direct — you don't need feedback to know this.
Not direct — network connectivity isn't part of what feedback evaluates.

scenario: 你平时能慢慢用 AI 完成题目，但正式面试有固定时长。
scenario_en: You can usually solve problems slowly with AI, but the real interview has a fixed time limit.
q: 练习时应该加入什么约束？
q_en: What constraint should you add during practice?
options: 无限时间直到写出完美答案再停
完全禁止运行任何测试
和真实面试匹配的计时器
只看题目，完全不动手写代码
options_en: Give yourself unlimited time until the answer is perfect.
Ban yourself from running any tests at all.
A timer that matches the real interview length.
Only read the problem and never actually write code.
why: 计时会强迫你在取向、规划、提示和验证之间做真实分配，这个分配是否可行只有掐着表才能暴露。
why_en: A realistic timer forces you to actually split time between orientation, planning, prompting, and verification, and only a clock reveals whether that split works.
whenOtherWins: 第一次熟悉工具时可以先不计时走一遍，之后就该尽快切到真实时间压力。
tradeoff: 计时暴露真实节奏 vs 不计时先求流程完整

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

optionMeanings: 去掉时间约束，练不出真实压力下的取舍。
把验证这一评估维度直接砍掉。
复刻正式面试最关键的资源约束：时间。
跳过写代码，练习本身就失去了意义。
optionMeanings_en: Removes the time constraint, so it never builds real-pressure tradeoffs.
Cuts out verification, one of the evaluated areas, entirely.
Recreates the most critical resource constraint of the real interview: time.
Skips writing code, which defeats the point of practicing at all.
optionScenarioImpacts: 没有截止时间，你不会暴露自己规划和验证的真实节奏。
不跑测试，AI 输出的隐藏 bug 不会被发现。
时间压力下才能看出提示、验证之间该怎么分配。
不写代码就没有可验证、可反馈的产出。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Without a deadline, your real planning and verification pace never gets exposed.
Skipping tests lets hidden bugs in AI output go undetected.
Only under time pressure do you see how to split prompting and verification.
No code means nothing verifiable to give feedback on.
optionDirectness: 不直接；时间正是这道题要补的约束。
不直接；测试是验证习惯的核心动作。
最直接；直接复刻了正式面试最关键的约束。
不直接；写代码是练习的基本前提。
optionDirectness_en: Not direct — time is exactly the constraint this practice needs to add.
Not direct — running tests is the core action of verification habits.
Most direct — it directly recreates the most critical constraint of the real interview.
Not direct — writing code is a basic precondition of practicing at all.

q: 把根据目标面试选择练习环境的逻辑排好：
q_en: Put the logic for choosing a practice environment by target interview in order:
steps: 优先选择对应格式的练习问题
识别目标面试是开放式还是结构化
在相同约束下计时完成
用反馈修正下一次练习
why: 准备要先确认目标面试的格式，再匹配题目和时间压力，最后用反馈闭环提高。
why_en: Preparation starts by identifying the target interview format, then matches problems and time pressure, and finally closes the loop with feedback.
tradeoff: 先定格式再分配练习资源 vs 不分格式统一刷题
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Target[Target company format] --> Structured{Structured?}
  Structured -->|yes| Browser[Practice browser flow]
  Structured -->|no| IDE[Practice own IDE]
  Browser --> Review[Review feedback]
  IDE --> Review

scenario: 开放式练习让你 clone 仓库到自己电脑，用日常工具和 AI 完整做完一题。
scenario_en: Open-ended practice has you clone a repo to your own machine and solve a full problem with your daily tools and AI.

options: 你自己的机器和编辑器
你日常使用的 AI 工具
从仓库开始构建并按真实时长计时
面试官预先写好的固定内置 AI 助手
options_en: Your own machine and editor.
The AI tools you use day to day.
Starting from the repo and timing yourself realistically.
A fixed built-in AI assistant chosen ahead of time by the interviewer.
why: 固定内置 AI 助手是结构化练习复刻的条件；开放式练的是你自己的机器、工具和真实时限。
why_en: A fixed built-in AI assistant belongs to structured practice; open-ended practice instead recreates your own machine, tools, and real time limit.

复刻你实际会用来驱动 AI 的工具选择。
复刻从零开始搭建加真实时间压力。
这是结构化练习复刻的条件，不属于开放式。

Recreates the actual AI tool choice you'd use to drive the work.
Recreates starting from scratch plus real time pressure.
This is what structured practice recreates, not open-ended.
optionScenarioImpacts: 机器和编辑器一致，工具摩擦不会在正式面试当天才暴露。
AI 工具一致，提示习惯可以直接迁移到面试。
从仓库起步加计时，复刻了任务规模和时间压力。
开放式练习里 AI 工具是你自选的，不是固定的。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Matching machine and editor means tool friction won't surprise you on the day.
Matching AI tools lets your prompting habits carry straight into the interview.
Starting from the repo with a timer recreates the real scope and time pressure.
In open-ended practice the AI tool is your own choice, not a fixed one.

Recreates the pacing of problems delivered in stages.

q: 开放式练习和结构化练习的核心区别是什么？
q_en: What is the core difference between open-ended and structured practice?
options: 开放式用自己的工具，结构化用平台锁定的浏览器内置工具
开放式不需要 AI，结构化不能写代码
开放式没有时间限制，结构化没有反馈

Open-ended doesn't need AI at all, and structured doesn't let you write code.
Open-ended has no time limit, and structured gives no feedback.

why: 两条通道的分界在于工具提供方：开放式用你自己的编辑器和 AI，结构化用平台锁定的浏览器沙盒和内置 AI。
why_en: The core difference is who provides the tools: open-ended uses your own editor and AI, while structured uses the platform's locked-down browser sandbox and built-in AI.
tradeoff: 复刻自带工具的真实工作流 vs 复刻平台锁定的受限环境

termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

凭空断言开放式不用 AI、结构化不能写代码。
凭空断言开放式没时限、结构化没反馈。
抹平了两者在环境和工具上的真实差异。
optionMeanings_en: Correctly names who provides the tools as the real dividing line.
Wrongly claims open-ended skips AI and structured skips coding.
Wrongly claims open-ended has no time limit and structured has no feedback.
Erases the real environment and tooling differences between the two.

两条通道其实都要写代码，也都能用 AI。
两条通道都设了计时和反馈机制。
如果真的一样，就不需要区分两条练习通道。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Different tool providers mean practice needs to recreate different environments.
Both tracks actually require writing code and both allow using AI.
Both tracks come with timing and feedback mechanisms.
If they were truly identical, there'd be no reason to split into two tracks.
optionDirectness: 最直接；这正是两条通道分设的原因。
不直接；两条通道都要写代码、都有 AI。

Not direct — both tracks require writing code and involve AI.

scenario: 练习反馈说你代码完成了，但 AI 聊天显示你多次接受了无法解释的实现。
scenario_en: Your practice feedback says the code was completed, but the AI chat shows you repeatedly accepted implementations you could not explain.
q: 下一轮练习最该改什么？
q_en: What should you change most in the next practice round?
options: 练习每次 AI 输出后，公开复述并解释关键实现逻辑
换更简单的题目，跳过阅读 AI 生成的代码
为了赶时间，直接停用所有单元测试
把精力全部放在更快点击提交按钮上
options_en: After every AI output, practice restating and explaining the key implementation logic out loud.
Switch to easier problems and skip reading the AI-generated code.
Turn off all unit tests to save time.
Put all your effort into clicking submit faster.
why: 反馈显示的是控制力缺口：能出代码不等于你在掌控实现；下一轮要练成每次输出后立刻复述解释。
why_en: The feedback points to a control gap, since finishing the code isn't the same as owning it, so next time practice narrating and explaining every AI output immediately.
whenOtherWins: 如果反馈主要是算法思路选错，就该回去补相关算法模式，而不是只练讲解习惯。
tradeoff: 每次输出后立即复述解释 vs 全盘接受不追问
codeSample:
After each AI output, say out loud:
1. What this code does: ...
2. Why I accept or reject it: ...
3. One thing I'd verify before moving on: ...

Cuts out verification entirely, making the risk worse.

An easier problem doesn't make you any better at explaining existing output.

Submitting faster doesn't prove you understood the code.

q: 补全准备原则：
q_en: Complete the preparation principle:
text: 准备 AI 编码面试不要只读内容；要在{{真实约束}}下练习，提交{{代码和聊天}}，再用{{反馈}}调整。
why: 只读内容学不到双线沟通和验证的节奏；在真实约束下练、把代码和聊天都交出去复盘，才能把知识变成能带上考场的工作流。
why_en: Reading alone can't teach the dual-conversation rhythm; only practicing under real constraints and reviewing both code and chat turns knowledge into an interview-day workflow.
